name: family_decrypt
description: Apply a recipe from stream_kpa_check (a key rule, a nonce and a cipher per member) to every member of an encrypted family, and give a receipt per member. RULES for an encrypted-file family (they are in every answer too): (1) measure what the encryptor added before hunting a key: a member against a same-name plaintext twin, the members against each other (encrypted_survey reports the overhead, the smallest member and whether the tails are unique per file); (2) read the encryption routine to the key's LAST use: where is the per-file key written? A constant-size trailer or header that is unique per file is where per-file key material is usually kept, often masked by a constant: test it (stream_kpa_check) before hunting memory; (3) one known (file, key) pair verifies any footer hypothesis; (4) a scan that finds nothing is a negative only after its planted control passed, and only for the shapes it lists. The chain, with no code to write: cipher_state_scan on a process dump (key and nonce candidates to a values file) -> stream_kpa_check on the encrypted files with that values file as key and nonce source (verdict per file, and the recipe) -> family_decrypt with the recipe file (every member, a receipt each). For each member the key is taken as the recipe says (a fixed value, or the member's own first or last bytes XORed with the recipe's constant), the payload (the file without the recipe's header_bytes and trailer_bytes) is XORed with the keystream of the member's cipher (ChaCha20 in either layout, Salsa20, AES-CTR, RC4 or repeating XOR, in pure Python), and the result is written to $OUT/decrypted/<number>_<name>, the name without its last extension when a known type stands before it (a.png.locked -> a.png). IT AUTHENTICATES NOTHING: a stream cipher has no integrity check and a wrong key also 'decrypts'. The one check made is whether the result starts with the bytes of the type the member's name promises: `decrypted, type confirmed` says only that; `decrypted, type not confirmed` says the name promises no known type or the result does not start like one, and what was written may then be noise. A member that is not in the recipe's assignments takes the variant whose result starts like its type, like any known type, or like text; when nothing tells the variants apart the first is used and the answer says so and is partial. Which files are members: `files`, or `dir` with `glob`; with dir and no glob, the recipe's member_suffix (the extension the checked members share) is the pattern, so a ransom note or a plaintext twin beside the members is not 'decrypted'. `status`: complete when every member named was decrypted and none promised a type its result does not show; partial when a member failed, a budget or the clock left members undone, a member's type was not confirmed against its name, or a variant was a default; failed when nothing was decrypted. Receipts: decrypt-receipts.jsonl under $OUT, one row per member decrypted or failed: sizes, the cipher and counter used, the sha256 of the member as it was and of the file written, the type the first bytes show, the verdict or the failure. The answer carries the same rows without the digest of the decrypted file. SENSITIVE: decrypted content is written, so the tool runs only in a job run as secret output (the manifest makes every job of this tool one); outside one it refuses and writes nothing. No key, nonce or mask byte and no plaintext byte is in the answer. Budgets: max_files (default 1000), max_bytes of payload in all (default 2 GiB, at most 64 GiB), max_seconds (default 1500, below the manifest's 1800). Measured, one core, Python 3.12 on an Apple M-series host, reading, hashing and writing included: Salsa20 about 22 MB/s, ChaCha20 about 16 MB/s, RC4 about 12 MB/s, AES-CTR about 10 MB/s; a job VM may be several times slower, so the default clock covers a few GB at best and a larger family needs several calls (give `files`). What a budget leaves undone is listed per member (`not decrypted`, with the reason); a member the clock stops midway has its partial output removed. A stop signal ends it with one JSON answer: partial when members were decrypted before it (each has its receipt and its file), failed when none was; the file being written at the stop is removed. A file already under $OUT is never replaced (a second name is taken). A link is not followed and only regular files are read; the evidence is opened read-only and never changed. Paths and file names are printed as given.

recipe_file.description: The recipe file stream_kpa_check wrote (its answer's recipe_file, e.g. store/jobs/j000013/out/stream-recipe.json). Give this or recipe

recipe.description: The recipe itself, as JSON: {"recipe": "stream-family/1", "key": {"hex": ...} or {"slice": "tail", "length": 32, "skip": 0, "xor_hex": ...}, "variants": [{"cipher": ..., "counter": 0, "nonce": {"hex": ...} or a slice or null}], "assignments": {name: variant number}, "header_bytes": 0, "trailer_bytes": 32, "member_suffix": ".locked"}. It holds key material and is recorded with the call: prefer recipe_file

files.description: Paths of the members to decrypt (1 to 100000). Give this or dir

dir.description: A directory holding the members; with glob and recursive. Give this or files

glob.description: A pattern on a file's name within dir (default: every name ending in the recipe's member_suffix, else "*")

recursive.description: true: also the directories below dir (no link followed). Default false

max_files.description: The most members decrypted (default 1000, at most 100000), in the order of their names

max_bytes.description: The most payload bytes decrypted in all (default 2147483648, at most 68719476736); a member that would pass it is listed as not decrypted

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 1500, at most 1740; the manifest's timeout is 1800)

limit.description: Member rows shown inline (default 200, at most 5000); every row is in the receipts file
